name: wc
description: Counts lines, words, and bytes (or characters) in files or input.

examples.explanation: The number of lines — for a log, the number of requests.
Counts items in the current directory.
Alternative to wc -l for counting matches: grep -c prints the count directly.

about: With no options wc prints all three counts: lines, words, bytes. When reading from a pipe there is no filename column, which is convenient in scripts: n=$(grep -c x file).
useCases: Count log entries, results, or files.
mistakes: Confusing -c (bytes) with -m (characters) on UTF-8 text — they differ when accents or emoji are present.
